This section gathers the AffineDrift tangent-space series on nonlinear dynamics, contraction-style reasoning, and related control questions. It is exploratory work. Some legacy page titles and file names still use the older "Tangent Hyperplane" label; this landing page uses "Tangent-Space Series" as the broader editorial label for the same material.

Multi-joint motion such as a golf swing is plainly nonlinear, yet this series calls some statements about it exact. The resolution is that each exact statement is either about one frozen instant or about first-order (vanishingly small) changes along one reference motion. The core thesis: for a differentiable model, at fixed state, time, and mode, perturbations map linearly to the first variation of the state rate. If the model is also control-affine, $\dot x=f_0(x,t)+G(x,t)u$, then a finite input increment $v$ changes the state rate by exactly $G(x,t)v$ while state, time and mode stay fixed, and the instantaneous force-to-acceleration map is affine in the declared input. In words: at that instant, the change in state rate is the input map times the change in input, however large the input change is. A taxi fare is a useful picture, with limits. A fare is a flag-drop plus a rate times the miles. Here the flag-drop is the acceleration that gravity and velocity-dependent forces produce with no input, and the rate card is the map from input to added acceleration. Because of the flag-drop, doubling the input need not double the acceleration, but extra input adds exactly the rate card times the extra input. Unlike a fare, the rate card is a matrix, so a push at one joint can change acceleration at others. And the picture holds only at one frozen instant and state (posture and velocity): when the state changes, both the flag-drop and the rate card change, so this does not make the whole motion linear. These are properties of the model and its derivatives; they do not establish biological intent, individual muscle recruitment, or optimal swing technique.

Here *mode* means the contact and constraint mode: which contacts and constraints are active, for example whether the clubhead is touching the ball. Within one mode the equations are smooth. Mode changes such as impacts, and other non-smooth events such as actuator saturation or friction transitions, need separate analysis; Part 6 treats impacts and mode changes. Finite-time conclusions require additional assumptions, residual bounds, and empirical validation where the argument is applied to measured movement.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Origin and Status

**State: Experimental.** This series is original AffineDrift synthesis and has not been peer reviewed. The exact instantaneous statements concern a single frozen instant, with state, time, constraints and contact mode held fixed. There, the first variation of the state rate is linear in the perturbation, and in control-affine models the force-to-acceleration map is affine in the input, so input increments add exactly. Along one reference motion, first variations also propagate linearly. None of this makes the nonlinear motion over a finite time (the finite-time flow) linear. Claims about force attribution, accumulation over time, and control design remain in-development arguments.
:::

## How to Read This Material

- **Start here:** the seven-part compact series below is the current editorial reading path. It supersedes the older standalone manuscript as the main reader journey; that designation is an editorial choice, not a comparative validation result.
- Use the [Critiques and Responses](../critiques/index.html) section alongside these pages; it contains the main limitations and objections that currently matter most.
- For deeper derivations (Hamiltonian/DDP/iLQR/MPC, case studies, appendices), see the full reference manuscript and the named advanced articles further down.

## Canonical Series

The seven-part compact series is the single canonical reading path. Each part builds on the previous one.

- [Part 1: Geometry](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-1-geometry.html): tangent spaces as exact infinitesimal descriptions, the exactness claim, and second-order residuals.
- [Part 2: Dynamics](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-2-dynamics.html): variational dynamics along a reference trajectory.
- [Part 3: Control](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-3-control.html): LQR, iLQR, and DDP as local methods on the moving tangent space.
- [Part 4: Residuals and Curvature](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-4-residuals-curvature.html): residual scaling and the limits of linearized predictions.
- [Part 5: Contraction](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-5-contraction.html): contraction certificates as tangent-space stability statements.
- [Part 6: Hybrid Systems](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-6-hybrid.html): saltation maps, mode changes, and the limits of smooth tangent reasoning.
- [Part 7: Residual-Aware Control](../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-7-residual-aware.html): residuals as trust-region, controller-switching, and validation signals.

## Full Reference Manuscript

- [Full Reference Manuscript: Exact Instantaneous Superposition in Nonlinear Dynamics](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-articles/Tangent_Hyperplanes_Unified_Thesis.html): the single-file reference manuscript. It restates the framework and adds the deep derivations (integral superposition, Hamiltonian/DDP/iLQR/MPC, case studies, appendices) that the compact series summarizes.

## Advanced / Reference Articles

These named articles develop specific advanced topics in depth. They are source-backed companions to the canonical series, not a parallel numbered reading path.

- [Contraction Theory Meets Tangent Spaces](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-articles/Advanced/Contraction_Tangent_Unification.html): source article behind compact Part 5, with longer derivations and implementation sketches.
- [Hybrid Tangent Spaces](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-articles/Advanced/Hybrid_Tangent_Spaces.html): source article behind compact Part 6, with saltation and contact-implicit detail.
- [Residual-Aware Control](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-articles/Advanced/Residual-Aware_Control.html): source article behind compact Part 7, with algorithm sketches and applications.

## Geometry Companion Articles

These standalone articles develop the mathematical machinery the series uses, treated at textbook length:

- [Superposition in Affine Control Systems](../articles/superposition.html): for control-affine models, the fixed-state force-to-acceleration map is affine, so input increments add exactly; the series' local statements build on this.
- [The Null Space of the Constraint Jacobian](../articles/null-space-constraint-jacobian.html): how constrained dynamics decompose into constrained and internal motion.
- [Force and Mobility Ellipsoids](../articles/force-mobility-matrices.html): the geometric reading of the state-dependent input map.
- [Degrees of Freedom and the Curse of Dimensionality](../articles/degrees-of-freedom-and-dimensionality.html): how constraints and structure collapse effective dimensionality.

## Scope Limits

- The strongest statements here are local statements about instantaneous mappings and linearized objects.
- Claims about finite-time superposition, accumulated error, or controller performance depend on how residual terms are bounded and how mode changes are handled.
- The hybrid and contraction-oriented extensions remain under active development.
